criteria_source: The fixture only. schema.sql stores every monetary column - plans.monthly_price, ledger_entries.amount, invoices.total - as DOUBLE PRECISION, and the trailing comment defines an account balance as sum(amount) over ledger_entries. IEEE 754 binary floating point cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly, so summing a ledger in it accumulates error; PostgreSQL 16 offers NUMERIC for this. The fact is about the database, not about rules/laconic.md.
trap: Passes when the answer names the DOUBLE PRECISION money columns as the defect to fix before a ledger is built on them - binary floating point cannot represent decimal amounts exactly, so a summed balance drifts - and points at NUMERIC/DECIMAL or integer minor units. Naming any one of the three money columns is enough. Fails when the answer calls the schema sound, or raises only the missing currency consistency constraint, indexing, the nullable canceled_at, the CHECK lists, normalization, or a missing updated_at while leaving the float money type unchallenged.
